scenario.title: Support backlog
scenario.initial_request: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds

M-IBAN-FAIL-RATE.name: Share of refund payments failing due to invalid IBAN format
M-IBAN-FAIL-RATE.numerator: refund payments with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT in payment-db
M-IBAN-FAIL-RATE.denominator: all refund payment attempts in payment-db
M-IBAN-FAIL-RATE.measurement_window: currently a 5-record sample (E-01); full-population measurement pending

M-SUPPORT-RESPONSE-MEDIAN.name: Median support ticket response time vs SLA

M-REFUND-FAIL-TICKET-VOLUME.name: Support tickets referencing refund status tied to IBAN-failed refunds
M-REFUND-FAIL-TICKET-VOLUME.population: DA-TCK tickets linked to FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT payment records

F-01.statement: All 5 queried refund records in payment-db failed with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT.

F-02.statement: Across 900 tickets, ticket-db reports a median response time of 2.0 hours against a 24-hour SLA.

CL-01.statement: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds

CL-02.statement: Customers wait forever; a chatbot would answer instantly.

H-LACK-SELF-SERVICE-ANSWERS.statement: Customers wait because there is no self-service channel to get refund status/answers, so they file tickets instead; a chatbot would resolve this.

H-SLOW-REFUND-PROCESSING.statement: The backlog stems from refunds actually taking too long to process (payment-db delays), so customers contact support about unresolved refunds, not merely a missing info channel.

H-SUPPORT-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: Ticket volume currently exceeds support team capacity, producing backlog and slow responses regardless of whether customers have self-service access.

H-NO-PROACTIVE-STATUS-UPDATES.statement: Customers contact support mainly because refund status is not proactively communicated to them, not because an answer channel is unavailable when they ask.

H-IBAN-FORMAT-FAILURES.statement: Refunds fail outright due to invalid IBAN format submitted/stored, causing customers whose refunds failed to contact support, independent of self-service availability or staffing.

interpretation_history.interpretation: payment-db shows all 5 sampled refund records failed with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, indicating a concrete payment-processing rejection reason rather than mere slowness or missing self-service information.

Across 900 tickets, the median support response time is 2.0 hours against a 24-hour SLA, indicating support is generally responding quickly rather than being systemically slow or backlogged. This weighs against capacity/speed-based explanations of the refund-wait complaint and is unrelated to the IBAN-format payment failures already identified.

E-03.content: Customers wait forever; a chatbot would answer instantly.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-SUP (support lead) restates the original request framing — customers wait and a chatbot would fix it — matching CL-01's already-recorded claim value, which is already contradicted by E-01's IBAN-format failure data. This is a non-authoritative reiteration, not new evidence, and is consistent with the stakeholder's noted bias toward framing everything as response speed.

U-IBAN-FAILURE-SHARE-OF-TICKET.question: What fraction of refund-related support tickets in ticket-db are actually tied to IBAN-format-failed payments in payment-db versus other causes?
U-IBAN-FAILURE-SHARE-OF-TICKET.decision_impact: Determines whether the fix should scope narrowly to IBAN validation/correction or whether a broader remediation is needed; a chatbot would not address this population either way.
U-IBAN-FAILURE-SHARE-OF-TICKET.resolution_path: Join ticket-db refund-related tickets with payment-db FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT records on refund/customer id and compute overlap share.
U-IBAN-FAILURE-SHARE-OF-TICKET.safe_placeholder: Scope the initial remediation to IBAN-format detection and correction only, without assuming it covers the full ticket volume.

U-CUSTOMER-NOTIFICATION-GAP.question: Are customers currently notified at all when their refund fails due to IBAN format, or do they only discover the failure by contacting support?
U-CUSTOMER-NOTIFICATION-GAP.decision_impact: Determines whether the fix needs a proactive notification step in addition to format correction.
U-CUSTOMER-NOTIFICATION-GAP.resolution_path: Inspect payment-db/ticket-db for any existing failure-notification records or handoffs tied to FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT events.
U-CUSTOMER-NOTIFICATION-GAP.safe_placeholder: Assume no notification currently exists and design the minimal fix to include an explicit failure notification.

U-PAYMENT-DATA-COMPLETENESS.question: Is payment-db's refund record set complete enough (completeness is UNKNOWN) for the 5-record sample to generalize to the full population?
U-PAYMENT-DATA-COMPLETENESS.decision_impact: Affects confidence in the iban_fail_rate metric and whether further sampling is needed before sizing the remediation.
U-PAYMENT-DATA-COMPLETENESS.resolution_path: Query payment-db for the full refund population size and failure-status breakdown rather than the 5-record sample.
U-PAYMENT-DATA-COMPLETENESS.safe_placeholder: Report iban_fail_rate as sample-based pending full-population confirmation.

A-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVE.statement: The 5 sampled refund records in payment-db (all FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT) are representative of the broader refund-wait complaint volume, not an unrepresentative small sample.

A-TICKETS-LINKED-TO-FAILURES.statement: The support tickets SH-SUP characterizes as a 'backlog' are substantially the same customers whose refunds failed on IBAN format, rather than an unrelated ticket population.

SC-ROOT-CAUSE-VALIDATED.statement: Refund-wait complaints are shown to be driven predominantly by IBAN-format payment failures rather than support slowness or missing self-service information.
SC-ROOT-CAUSE-VALIDATED.threshold: majority of sampled refund-related tickets correspond to FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT records
SC-ROOT-CAUSE-VALIDATED.validation_method: Join ticket-db refund tickets with payment-db failure records and compute the overlap share against E-01's sample.

SC-TICKET-REDUCTION.statement: Support tickets about refund status decrease after IBAN-format failures are corrected and customers are notified.
SC-TICKET-REDUCTION.validation_method: Compare refund_fail_ticket_volume in ticket-db before and after remediation deployment.

VOB-U-IBAN-FAILURE-SHARE-OF-TICKET.unresolved_question: What fraction of refund-related support tickets in ticket-db are actually tied to IBAN-format-failed payments in payment-db versus other causes?
VOB-U-IBAN-FAILURE-SHARE-OF-TICKET.reason_deferred: deferred at DEFINE Gate; safe placeholder: Scope the initial remediation to IBAN-format detection and correction only, without assuming it covers the full ticket volume.
VOB-U-IBAN-FAILURE-SHARE-OF-TICKET.validation_method: Join ticket-db refund-related tickets with payment-db FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT records on refund/customer id and compute overlap share.

VOB-U-CUSTOMER-NOTIFICATION-GAP.unresolved_question: Are customers currently notified at all when their refund fails due to IBAN format, or do they only discover the failure by contacting support?
VOB-U-CUSTOMER-NOTIFICATION-GAP.reason_deferred: deferred at DEFINE Gate; safe placeholder: Assume no notification currently exists and design the minimal fix to include an explicit failure notification.
VOB-U-CUSTOMER-NOTIFICATION-GAP.validation_method: Inspect payment-db/ticket-db for any existing failure-notification records or handoffs tied to FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT events.

VOB-R-3.unresolved_question: Can write/deploy access to payment-db (for IBAN validation) and ticket-db (for notifications) be granted or provisioned, or must implementation of the structural fixes be fully handed off to the owning engineering team outside this harness?

VOB-R-3.validation_method: Confirm with platform/engineering owners whether a write-capable tool or deployment pipeline exists or can be provisioned for payment-db and ticket-db changes, and on what timeline.

Engineering team confirmation of handoff acceptance and implementation timeline for SR-IBAN-VALIDATION-AT-SUBMISSIO

problem_definition.requested_solution: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds (SH-SUP's initial framing, CL-01/CL-02) — rejected as the mechanism; the chatbot/self-service premise is contradicted by the confirmed IBAN-failure cause.
symptoms: Support lead reports customers wait and files a backlog/response-speed complaint about refunds (initial request, CL-01/CL-02)
All 5 sampled refund records in payment-db failed with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01, F-01)
Across 900 tickets, median support response time is 2.0h against a 24h SLA, i.e. support itself is not slow (E-02, F-02)
problem_definition.root_problem: Refund payments are failing outright because the submitted/stored IBAN format is invalid (payment-db status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, E-01, F-01), and affected customers then contact support seeking resolution of their stuck refund — not because support is slow (median 2.0h vs 24h SLA, E-02) or because a self-service answer channel is missing.

trace.summary: Refund payments are failing outright because the submitted/stored IBAN format is invalid (payment-db status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, E-01, F-01), and affected customers then contact support seeking resolution of their stuck refund — not because support is slow (median 2.0h vs 24h SLA, E-02) or because a self-service answer channel is missing.

details.requested_solution: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds (SH-SUP's initial framing, CL-01/CL-02) — rejected as the mechanism; the chatbot/self-service premise is contradicted by the confirmed IBAN-failure cause.

trace.summary: Agent judgment is needed only where ticket-db records lack a clean structured key to payment-db refund IDs, requiring interpretation to match tickets to FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT records; the core join itself is a deterministic read-only query.

structural_remedies.description: Add format validation of IBAN at the point of submission/storage in the refund payment process so invalid IBANs are rejected or corrected before processing, matching intended_scope action validate_iban_before_submission:DA-PAY.
structural_remedies.rationale: Specifying the validation rule is feasible in the remaining 225 minutes, but scenario.tool_surface lists payment-db as read_only; no write/deploy tool exists in this harness to implement the change.; residual gap: Actual code/config deployment must be handed off to the owning engineering team outside this harness's current read-only tool access.

structural_remedies.description: Add a process/ownership change so customers are proactively notified when their refund status becomes FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, matching intended_scope action notify_customers_of_failed_refund:DA-TCK, instead of them discovering the failure by filing a ticket.
structural_remedies.rationale: Designing the notification trigger is feasible in time, but ticket-db is read_only per tool_surface, so no tool here can send notifications; also U-CUSTOMER-NOTIFICATION-GAP/VOB-U-CUSTOMER-NOTIFICATION-GAP is still OPEN, so current notification state is unverified.; residual gap: Requires write capability outside current tool surface plus resolution of VOB-U-CUSTOMER-NOTIFICATION-GAP before this can be specified precisely.

structural_remedies.description: Run a deterministic join of ticket-db refund tickets against payment-db FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT records (per SC-ROOT-CAUSE-VALIDATED's validation_method) to quantify overlap and close VOB-U-IBAN-FAILURE-SHARE-OF-TICKET, matching intended_scope action analyze_refund_failure_scope.
structural_remedies.rationale: Both payment-db and ticket-db are HEALTHY and read_only is sufficient for a read-only join/query; no write access is needed for this analysis.; residual gap: If ticket records lack a clean structured key to the refund/payment record, matching individual tickets to failures may be ambiguous rather than a simple deterministic join.

decision_log.rationale: causal chain: Customer initiates a refund whose IBAN is in an invalid format at intake → Payment processing rejects the refund with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT in payment-db (E-01, F-01) → The failed refund is not resolved, so the customer perceives themselves as 'waiting' and files/escalates a support ticket seeking resolution → Support lead observes the resulting tickets and frames the pattern as a response-speed/self-service gap (CL-01/CL-02, E-03), even though response time itself is within SLA (E-02, F-02); rejected framings: [('H-LACK-SELF-SERVICE-ANSWERS', 'Only supported by E-03, a non-authoritative restatement of the initial stakeholder request from SH-SUP (noted bias toward response-speed framing); the confirmed concrete cause is IBAN-format payment failure (E-01), not absence of a self-service channel.'), ('H-SLOW-REFUND-PROCESSING', 'REJECTED in state: contradicted by E-01, which shows outright failure (FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT) rather than delayed processing.'), ('H-SUPPORT-STAFFING-SHORTAGE', 'REJECTED in state: contradicted by E-02, which shows median response time (2.0h) well within the 24h SLA across 900 tickets.'), ('H-NO-PROACTIVE-STATUS-UPDATES', 'CANDIDATE with no supporting evidence cited; not adopted as the premise, though the related notification question is carried forward as an unknown.')]

[CONDITIONAL] critical unknown U-IBAN-FAILURE-SHARE-OF-TICKET deferred to VOB-U-IBAN-FAILURE-SHARE-OF-TICKET; [CONDITIONAL] critical unknown U-CUSTOMER-NOTIFICATION-GAP deferred to VOB-U-CUSTOMER-NOTIFICATION-GAP

proposal.root_problem: Refund payments are failing outright because the submitted/stored IBAN format is invalid (payment-db status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, E-01, F-01), and affected customers then contact support seeking resolution of their stuck refund — not because support is slow (median 2.0h vs 24h SLA, E-02) or because a self-service answer channel is missing.
proposal.requested_solution: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds (SH-SUP's initial framing, CL-01/CL-02) — rejected as the mechanism; the chatbot/self-service premise is contradicted by the confirmed IBAN-failure cause.
symptoms: Support lead reports customers wait and files a backlog/response-speed complaint about refunds (initial request, CL-01/CL-02)
All 5 sampled refund records in payment-db failed with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01, F-01)
Across 900 tickets, median support response time is 2.0h against a 24h SLA, i.e. support itself is not slow (E-02, F-02)
causal_chain: Customer initiates a refund whose IBAN is in an invalid format at intake
Payment processing rejects the refund with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT in payment-db (E-01, F-01)
The failed refund is not resolved, so the customer perceives themselves as 'waiting' and files/escalates a support ticket seeking resolution
Support lead observes the resulting tickets and frames the pattern as a response-speed/self-service gap (CL-01/CL-02, E-03), even though response time itself is within SLA (E-02, F-02)

assumptions.statement: The 5 sampled refund records in payment-db (all FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT) are representative of the broader refund-wait complaint volume, not an unrepresentative small sample.
The support tickets SH-SUP characterizes as a 'backlog' are substantially the same customers whose refunds failed on IBAN format, rather than an unrelated ticket population.

unknowns.resolution_path: Join ticket-db refund-related tickets with payment-db FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT records on refund/customer id and compute overlap share.
unknowns.safe_placeholder: Scope the initial remediation to IBAN-format detection and correction only, without assuming it covers the full ticket volume.

unknowns.question: Are customers currently notified at all when their refund fails due to IBAN format, or do they only discover the failure by contacting support?

unknowns.resolution_path: Inspect payment-db/ticket-db for any existing failure-notification records or handoffs tied to FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT events.
unknowns.safe_placeholder: Assume no notification currently exists and design the minimal fix to include an explicit failure notification.

unknowns.decision_impact: Affects confidence in the iban_fail_rate metric and whether further sampling is needed before sizing the remediation.
unknowns.resolution_path: Query payment-db for the full refund population size and failure-status breakdown rather than the 5-record sample.
